title: Zero to one for field operations
subtitle: Designing a new product category for crews who work with gloves on, outdoors, offline
role: Head of Product Design — founding design hire
summary: Built the design practice and shipped v1 of a field-operations app for logistics crews, from first customer interviews through a 40-site rollout.

sections.heading: Designing for a screen no one asked for
body: Fieldnote's crews had never used a work app before — job assignments came from a radio call and a paper ticket. I was the first design hire, joining pre-product-market-fit, and my first job wasn't screens, it was figuring out whether a screen was even the right answer.

I spent three weeks riding along with crews across two sites before opening a design tool. The biggest early finding: gloves, glare, and one-handed use ruled out most conventional mobile patterns outright.

sections.heading: Designing for the worst network you've ever used
body: Crews worked in warehouses and rural sites with unreliable connectivity. Every interaction had to work offline first and sync opportunistically — which meant rethinking basic patterns like 'saving' and 'submitting' as background, resilient operations rather than user-triggered network calls with loading states.

This constraint shaped the whole information architecture: instead of a screen-per-task model, we built around a persistent local job queue that crews could act on regardless of connection, with sync status expressed as ambient UI rather than blocking dialogs.

sections.heading: Scaling the design practice alongside the product
body: As the team grew from 1 to 3 designers, I wrote the first version of Fieldnote's component guidelines directly from the shipped v1 UI rather than as an upfront system — documenting real, tested patterns instead of speculative ones. That library became the foundation for the design system a later platform team formalized.
By the end of year one we'd rolled out to 40 sites, and I'd hired and was managing the two designers who took over day-to-day ownership of the crew-facing app while I moved on to dispatch tooling.
